driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of 2 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions pre-open fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-10-01.json from Thursday 1 October's close. Every figure is dated at or before the 2026-10-01 close; news-log entries dated 2 October (September payrolls, crude slide) were deliberately not used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale: bonds 15 (TLT 30-day implied volatility, 25 September), dollar 4.72 (EUR/USD 1-month implied volatility, 21 September), IWM 19.97 (RVX, 23 September). No newer prints were obtainable.

Source conflicts on 1 October: the news log has the S&P 500 cash index at 7,673.89 (+0.29%) while a second wrap shows 7,666.45 (+0.19%), and the drafted ES=F close is -0.15%; gold is -0.39% on the drafted GC=F close while one wrap shows spot gold up about 0.5%; votes use the drafted closes and avoid the conflicting levels.

No 1 October high-yield OAS, MOVE, or positioning print was obtainable; credit, positioning and volatility votes are neutral where no dated figure exists. AAII (32.7/19.2/48.1) is the week to 23 September. Seasonality votes are neutral because no dated sourced statistic was obtained.

Fed odds: October hike probability was roughly 50% after Williams' 30 September remarks (single source). Calendar: the September jobs report is due 2 October, after the close of this window and not used.

News-log entries for 2026-10-01 (yields at multi-decade highs, Micron-led chip rally, oil/Brent above $100, close, Broadcom-Anthropic financing, ISM manufacturing) were already in data/news_log.json; the Artifact database returned the same six entries. No hand-entered issue entries were dated 1 October.

newsLog.event: US 10Y Treasury yield jumps to highest since April 2002 and 30Y to highest since July 2002 as global yields surge; European stocks start Q4 lower
newsLog.reaction: Pressure on bonds and rate-sensitive equities; Europe weaker, US futures still bid on AI/chip strength

newsLog.event: Micron blockbuster results and guidance spark global semiconductor/AI rally; Nikkei and Kospi surge, Nvidia/AMD/Broadcom higher pre-market
newsLog.numbers: Micron revenue ~4x y/y; Nikkei +2.9%; Kospi +1.3%; S&P fut +0.3%; Nasdaq-100 fut +0.6%; Dow fut +0.2% (+86 pts)
newsLog.reaction: Chip squeeze lifts tech; Nasdaq futures lead; Micron itself muted after +270% YTD run
newsLog.vsExp: Revenue and guidance above expectations (figures n/a)

newsLog.event: Crude rallies with Brent back above $100 while US-Iran diplomatic backchannels continue; adds to inflation/yield worries
newsLog.reaction: Higher oil feeds inflation and rate fears; supportive for energy, a headwind for broad equities and bonds

newsLog.event: US stocks close modestly higher to start Q4 as Treasury yields retreat from a 24-year intraday high; Micron-led chip strength supports Nasdaq
newsLog.reaction: All three major indexes finished in the green as yields eased off two-decade highs; S&P led gains, chip stocks extended Micron-driven rally

newsLog.event: Broadcom agrees to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion via convertible notes to help finance AI chip/TPU leasing ahead of Anthropic's expected IPO
newsLog.numbers: $42B financing vs. $125.2B five-year TPU compute commitment; Broadcom shares -1.10%
newsLog.reaction: AVGO dips slightly amid flagged conflict-of-interest concerns (lender and chip supplier in one), even as deal deepens Broadcom-Anthropic compute tie-up ahead of a reported $2T+ IPO valuation target

newsLog.event: September ISM Manufacturing PMI registers 54.5%, a ninth straight month of expansion, but the Prices Index jumps sharply on tariff/metals costs
newsLog.numbers: PMI 54.5% (Aug 54.6%); New Orders 55.3% (+1.6pt); Employment 52.7% (+1.5pt); Prices Index 77.9% (+6.8pt)
newsLog.reaction: Resilient factory activity reinforces soft-landing narrative but rising input costs add to inflation/tariff concerns already pressuring yields
newsLog.vsExp: Roughly in line with prior month (-0.1pt m/m)
